response.sql: WITH district_counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), district_shares AS (SELECT district_id, account_count, account_count * 1.0 / SUM(account_count) OVER () AS share FROM district_counts), results AS (SELECT district_id, account_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_above_average FROM district_shares) SELECT district_id, account_count, share, share_above_average FROM results ORDER BY share_above_average DESC, district_id ASC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: When districts tie, the lower district id comes first to choose exactly 10 rows.
